1. Financial health of the business

  • On the top left we can observed the premiums and claims outflow from the business.

  • On the top right, we also observe the net profit margin has slowed significantly since 2023 to 2024

  • Lastly, we are receiving lower average premiums per exposure year. This signals we need to relook at how we are pricing our policies

2. Product profitability

  • In this slide, we observed 2 critical observation.

A performance review of the product portfolio reveals a dangerous concentration risk, with over 80% of total premiums heavily reliant on just two offerings: Third Party (2 or more coverage) and Comprehensive with Excess.

The remaining product lines demonstrate severe profitability distress.

Comprehensive without Excess is currently operating at an breakeven. Concurrently, Third Party with Glass Coverage and basic Third Party plans are yielding razor-thin margins, failing to contribute meaningfully to the bottom line despite their operational footprint.

We will further investigate the cause for these 3 portfolios in subsequent slides.

3. Total Premiums payment over the years Comprehensive without Excess

Note: The scale is in log, but the x axis is in actual dollars

Key insight: Comprehensive insurance without excess shows a stable distribution for both premiums and claims from 2022 through 2024, explaining why it is barely making a profit on an aggregate level. Crucially, the multi-peaked distributions across all years confirm the existence of distinct customer sub-groups (e.g., a distinct low-premium tier and a high-premium tier).

Because year-over-year premium growth has remained stagnant, strategic adjustments are required. Further monitoring and tweaking of this policy are needed to intentionally pull more customers into the higher-tier, higher-margin brackets to improve profitability.”

4. Total Premiums payment over the years Third-Party with Glass Cov

Note: The scale is in log, but the x axis is in actual dollars

Third-Party with Glass Coverage shows an increasing volume of lower-priced premiums over the years, though the median premium remains stable around $200 On the claims side, while the median has held steady at approximately $1,000 from 2022 to 2024, the structure of the risk has shifted significantly. Claims have become much more heavily concentrated right at the $1,000 mark in 2024, alongside a wider variation of smaller claims emerging below the 25th percentile.

Based on the shifting claims structure, it is highly recommended to conduct a targeted risk and underwriting review focused on two areas

5. Total Premiums payment over the years Basic Third-Party

Note: The scale is in log, but the x axis is in actual dollars

The premium structure for this plan experienced significant compression in 2024, shifting away from the wider variations of previous years into a distinct bimodal distribution.

This structural change strongly indicates the emergence of two polarized risk segments or sub-groups within the same product line, even though the overall average premium level has stabilized between 2023 and 2024.

Concurrently, the portfolio’s claim experience underwent a critical upward migration. While prior years were dominated by low-value “background” claims, 2024 losses heavily bottlenecked near a much higher median payout while maintaining highly volatile outer boundaries.

This combination of a rising baseline cost per claim warrants a review of this insurance policy.

6. Types of claims per low profitability portfolios

The Comprehensive without Excess plan exhibits widespread, high-frequency claims, with severe activation bands across Property, Glass, and Liability Property claims

In stark contrast, Third-Party with Two or More Coverages shows a highly localized, sparse risk profile, with claims strictly concentrated within third-party property and bodily injury liabilities, indicating a lower-frequency but potentially higher-severity exposure.

For Basic Third-Party policies, claims are almost exclusively restricted to a vertical band of liability protection. This pattern aligns precisely with Spanish legal mandates, where entry-level insurance operates under Responsabilidad Civil Obligatoria

7. Profile of Driver and Vehicle age against claims without Excess

There is a distinct pricing mismatch within the Third-Party with two or more Coverages portfolio. While underwriting successfully charges a steep risk premium on young drivers (18–25) and brand-new vehicles (0–3 years), it severely underprices the mid-aged driver segment (36–55) operating mid-age vehicles (4–6 years).

This exact underpriced demographic is likely to be driving the portfolio’s exposure, peaking at a 37.1% claim frequency. To stabilize the portfolio’s margin, the underwriting team should review the pricing tiers upward for drivers aged 36–55 who operate vehicles under 6 years old.

8. Profile of Driver and Vehicle age against claims Third Party with two or more coverage

While the pricing structure successfully accounts for high-risk young drivers (18–25), it completely fails to protect against a major risk spike in senior operators.

Drivers aged 66+ operating 4–6 year old vehicles generate the portfolio’s highest liability claim rate at 26.1%, yet this demographic pays below-average baseline premiums. Because basic plans have thin margins by design, this unpriced exposure severely compromises the product’s profitability.

9. Profile of Driver and Vehicle age against claims Basic Third party

The underwriter successfully priced in premiums for the 18-25 age groups with newer vehicles from 0 -6 years.

However, a critical underwriting leakage exists in the mature segment: drivers aged 56–65 operating 7–10 year old cars run a highly elevated 21.4% claim rate, yet they are granted below-average premium rates.

10. Vehicle Type and District claim rate

Our high-volume segments (left) exhibit a stable, controlled claim rate of approximately 10-12%, However, the treemap reveals significant risk volatility in our low-volume, niche segments (bottom-right), where claim rates swing drastically up to 25%. This indicates a need to either consolidate these micro-segments or apply stricter pricing loading to these volatile pockets.”

11. Data Issues

Missing values in vehicle_value and fuel_type stem from systematic pipeline anomalies rather than random omissions. Engineering investigation is underway; missing fields were temporarily imputed to preserve data integrity for modeling

12. Conclusion

Overall Findings

  • Over 80% of total premium revenue is reliant on just two offerings: Third-Party two or more coverages and Comprehensive with Excess.

  • Year-on-year premium growth has flattened, and we are receiving a lower average premium per exposure year across the business, signaling an urgent need to relook at baseline pricing.

Plug Critical Underwriting Price Leakages

Granular subgroup analysis reveals that while high-risk young drivers (\(18\text{--}25\)) are priced correctly, we are severely underpricing specific high-risk mature demographics:

  • Drivers aged \(36\text{--}55\) operating vehicles aged \(4\text{--}6\) years peak at a massive 37.1% claim frequency but are currently charged below-average premiums.
